items.summary: The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court recently observed that doctors refuse to perform abortions even in cases where the procedure is legally permitted under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act. Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani made the comment while dealing with a case of a woman who, despite serious foetal abnormalities, had to approach the Court for medical termination of pregnancy after doctors refused to perform abortion without judicial order. The Court emphasised that medical practitioners should not unnecessarily avoid attending emergent cases for which statutory directions under the MTP Act and relevant rules are clear. items.title: What happens after Delhi Police detains you? I saw it first hand
items.summary: Delhi Police is beating protesters after detaining them. I saw this firsthand while sitting inside the blue, mesh-windowed van the police usually uses to ferry prisoners and undertrials between prisons and courts. Detained on Sunday evening, I saw three policemen pummel almost everyone who boarded after me: two stood at the van’s door at the back, and the third inside the corridor, which opened into mesh-covered, cage-like enclosures. Once each citizen entered the corridor, they were hit in the abdomen, elbowed hard in the back, kicked and worse. One youngster was pushed to the floor and beaten there. Another was viciously stamped on. These assaults were systematic, seemed to last roughly similar lengths of time for each person being detained, and served as the prologue to the shove into the cages. Earlier that evening, at around 4 pm, while sloganeering against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, a small group of student protesters from Disha Student Union (Disha Chhatra Sangathan) was intercepted by Delhi Police at the junction of Panchkuian Road and Outer Circle at Connaught Place in central Delhi. items.title: Personality Rights vs Freedom of Expression - Finding a balance
items.summary: John Stuart Mill The only freedom which deserves the name, is that of pursuing our own good in our own way, so long as we do not attempt to deprive others of theirs, or impede their efforts to obtain it. Freedom of speech and expression has long been regarded as a cornerstone of constitutional democracy. In India, it is guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India, 1950, and embodies the liberty to communicate ideas, share information, and engage in creative expression. Yet, freedom of speech and expression has never been understood to be absolute. During the Constituent Assembly debates, members grappled with the limits of fundamental rights and recognised the need to reconcile individual liberty with competing interests. The significance of this debate continues to hold relevance even today, particularly when the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression overlaps and traverses with other fundamental rights. items.title: You ate his ear off, how do we replace it? Supreme Court to man seeking bail in assault case
items.summary: "You ate his ear, how do we replace it?" the Supreme Court asked a man on Wednesday, giving short shrift to his petition for anticipatory bail in an assault case. Injecting a dose of dry judicial wit into the hearing, a Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran made it clear that a litigant accused of chomping off a neighbour's ear during a street clash could hardly expect pre-arrest protection. The matter reached the top court on an appeal challenging a February 2026 order of the Jharkhand High Court, which had refused anticipatory bail to one Rajiv Ranjan Kumar over a violent clash in Ranchi. Kumar's counsel attempted to soften the blow by painting the incident as a routine neighbourhood feud that simply spiralled out of control on a festive night. "It’s a long-simmering dispute between neighbours. It flared up on one night and cross-FIRs were registered. The opposite side managed to get anticipatory bail while I was denied the same. The way it started was, it was the night of Janmashtami, people were celebrating and there was some stone pelting..." the counsel submitted. items.title: Adani Green Energy moves Karnataka High Court against 1% property tax on solar power plants
items.summary: Adani Green Energy (UP) Limited (petitioner) has approached the Karnataka High Court challenging the State government's amended rules imposing property tax at the rate of 1 percent of the property's value on solar power plants. The company has challenged the Karnataka Grama Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Grama Panchayat Taxes, Rates and Fees) Rules, 2025, notified on October 17, 2025 to the extent they classify solar power plants as regular industrial buildings for taxation purposes. It has also sought the quashing of demand notices and assessment proceedings initiated by the concerned gram panchayat authorities for the assessment year 2026-27. The petitioner has contended that solar power plants constitute a distinct category of infrastructure and cannot be equated with conventional industrial buildings for the purpose of levying property tax. According to the petition, the government had earlier prescribed a tax of ₹5,000 per megawatt per annum for renewable energy units, including solar power plants, following recommendations made by an expert committee constituted to examine taxation issues affecting small-scale industries. items.title: Farmers, Workers to Intensify Struggle, ‘Jail Bharo’ on Aug 10
items.summary: At a joint convention held in Delhi recently, farmer and worker organisations announced a countrywide ‘Jail Bharo’ agitation to voice their longstanding demands.

items.title: Left Groups Protest Workers' Repression in North India
items.summary: Left groups held strong protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in support of the workers' movement and against police repression in North India.
